pricing.title: Pricing policy
pricing.description: The engine converts currency first, then applies the base rate, market rules, and priority exceptions. Guardrails and rounding are applied last.

help.engine: The backend calculates price deterministically: catalog, currency, base rate, shop type, transport, stock and demand, season, wealth, legality, reputation, policy, exceptions, GM adjustment and guardrails. The interface does not duplicate calculations. Every step is visible in the breakdown tab.
help.basics: Base rates start retail and buyback, while value thresholds classify goods for later rules. They do not replace shop type, demand or condition. Typical retail is 100–140% and buyback 35–70% of catalog.
help.saleRate: Base player price is applied after currency conversion and before market rules. It does not alter catalog price. Typical range is 100–140%; current {value}%. A catalog value of 100 at 120% gives a base of 120.
help.buybackRate: Base buyback rate sets the shop's starting payout before condition, demand and capital limits. It does not affect retail. Typical range is 35–70%; current {value}%.
help.minimumPrice: Minimum price runs last and protects against a zero or negative result. It does not raise prices already above the floor. Zero to five smallest units is typical; current {value}.
help.roundingStep: Rounding step aligns the final result to convenient denominations. It does not change earlier multipliers. One, five or ten is typical; current {value}. A step of 5 moves 137 to 135 or 140 depending on direction.
help.roundingMode: Direction decides whether the engine uses the nearest, always higher or always lower step. It does not affect availability. Current: {value}.
help.priceBand: The “{label}” threshold classifies an item by its converted price. It affects wealth rules and exceptions but does not itself change price. Current threshold: {value}. Thresholds should increase in order.
help.presets: A preset applies a coherent set of rates, guardrails and enabled rules. It does not alter the world profile or stock. Manual changes create a custom policy that can be saved under a new name.
help.currency: Settlement currency and rates run before margin. A fee applies only when currencies differ. A price already stored in the shop currency is not converted again.
help.settlementCurrency: Settlement currency defines the final price unit and matching purse. It does not change value without a rate. Current: {value}. For example, silver prices are converted to the shop's pennies first.
help.buyFee: Purchase fee is added only when item and shop currencies differ. It does not apply to buyback. Typical range is 0–10%; current {value}%.
help.sellFee: Buyback fee is deducted only when exchanging foreign currency. It does not affect the buyer's price. Typical range is 0–10%; current {value}%.
help.exchangeRate: The rate says how many smallest units of “{target}” equal one unit of “{source}”. It contains no margin or fee. It must be positive; current {value}. A rate of 2 converts 10 to 20 before later rules.
help.guardrails: Guardrails constrain extreme results after modifiers and prevent buyback above retail. They do not replace sound configuration. A GM exception can bypass them only when explicitly enabled.
help.guardrailsEnabled: The switch activates every configured limit. Disabling it preserves values but permits arbitrarily extreme prices. Current: {value}. Guardrails should normally remain active.
help.guardrail: “{label}” constrains a calculated result only when it crosses the bound. It does not alter a price inside the range. Current: {value}. Detail: {hint}
help.modifiers: Market rules enable only factors meaningful for a given item. Disabling one removes its price impact and breakdown step but does not change profile data.
help.modifier: Rule “{label}”: {description} Its impact depends on the item and can be skipped when irrelevant. Current: {value}. The simulator shows a concrete application or skip.
help.exceptions: A GM exception applies only when every non-empty criterion matches. It can multiply, add a fixed amount or set a fixed price. Other goods remain unchanged; higher priority runs first.
help.exceptionPicker: The list selects one exception for editing so the form stays compact. It does not change rule order or behavior. Calculation order still follows priority.
help.exceptionActive: A disabled rule keeps its configuration but is skipped during calculation. It does not affect other exceptions. Use this for temporary variant testing.
help.exceptionPriority: Higher priority runs first. It is not a price multiplier. −100 to 100 is typical; current {value}. Ties keep a stable rule order.
help.exceptionModes: Modes decide whether the exception applies to retail, buyback or both. They do not alter other operations. At least one mode must remain active.
help.exceptionCriterion: Criterion “{field}” currently has “{value}”. Empty or “any” adds no restriction. Every configured criterion must match together; other goods remain unchanged.
help.exceptionEffect: Effect type chooses a percentage multiplier, fixed surcharge or discount, or fixed price. It runs only after criteria match. Fixed price replaces the result; other effects adjust it.
help.exceptionEffectValue: The value sets the selected effect's strength; current {value}. For a multiplier, 100 means unchanged; for an adjustment, 0 changes nothing. Guardrails still apply unless explicitly bypassed.
help.exceptionStop: After this rule matches, the engine can skip lower-priority exceptions. It does not stop earlier market stages or final guardrails.
help.exceptionIgnoreGuardrails: Allows this rule to bypass global price bounds. It does not disable invalid or negative number validation. Use only for an intentional narrative price.
help.exceptionSuppress: Selected general rules are skipped only when this exception matches. They remain active for other goods. An official price might suppress demand and reputation.
help.quickTest: Representative test calculates several selected goods together to reveal effects across categories. It saves nothing and does not alter stock.
help.previewTemplate: The item supplies catalog data, currency, category, legality and current stock for the test. It is not added to the offer and no price is saved. The current choice is visible in the field; test both ordinary and luxury goods.
help.previewMode: Mode selects retail to a player or buyback from a player because they use different rates, stock rules and limits. It does not change the saved policy.
help.previewQuantity: Quantity calculates batch value and can trigger the buyback budget limit. It does not multiply unit price before modifiers. Preview range is 1–9999 and the choice is only a test.
help.previewCondition: Physical condition changes valuation, especially during buyback. It does not alter catalog price or category availability. Good is neutral; ruined usually cuts value sharply.
help.previewReputation: Relationship simulates terms for a particular buyer or seller. It does not alter base shop reputation. Neutral is the baseline and an individual relationship may override it.
help.previewTemporary: Temporary GM adjustment runs after policy and exceptions but before guardrails and rounding. It is not saved to the profile. −20 to +20% is a typical test; the guardrail sets the limit.

presets.title: Policy assignment
presets.description: Choose a ready-made policy for this shop. Manual policy changes create a custom policy; no assignment means the general rules apply.

general.label: General rules
general.description: No policy is assigned to this shop. The world's safe general rules are applied.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.description: Default trade with 60% buyback and arbitrage protection.

friendly.label: Player-friendly
friendly.description: Lower retail prices and a more favorable buyback rate.

premium.label: Premium
premium.description: Higher margins, cautious buyback, and wider price bounds.

unrestricted.label: Free market
unrestricted.description: No global bounds; GM rules have full control.

custom.label: Custom policy
custom.description: These settings were adjusted manually for this particular shop.

basics.title: Base rates and value scale
basics.description: Values are system-neutral and work with pennies, dollars, credits, or any other canonical currency unit.
basics.saleRateHint: 100% means the catalog price before market rules.
basics.buybackRateHint: Catalog price percentage paid before further adjustments.
basics.minimumPriceHint: Use 0 if free items are allowed.
basics.roundingStepHint: For example, 5 rounds to multiples of five canonical units.

priceBandHints.cheapMax: Items below this amount are in the cheapest value band.
priceBandHints.midMax: Upper bound for ordinary items in settlement currency.
priceBandHints.highMax: Items above this amount are treated as luxury goods.

currency.title: Currencies and exchange
currency.description: Each source price is converted into one settlement currency before margins are applied. This safely combines regional coinage or currencies from different settings.
currency.settlementHint: The shop displays prices and settles the matching hero purse in this currency. The change takes effect after saving the shop profile.
currency.buyFeeHint: Added when the item currency differs from the settlement currency.
currency.sellFeeHint: Deducted from payouts involving foreign currency.
currency.paymentExchangeFeeHint: Added to the amount charged from the hero's foreign-currency purse.
currency.ratesHint: A rate is the number of smallest settlement units per one smallest source-currency unit.
currency.rateUnit: 1 unit of {source} = rate × one unit of {target}
currency.missingRate: No saved rate exists for this item's currency. The preview temporarily assumes 1:1; set a rate before opening the shop.

guardrails.title: Economic guardrails
guardrails.description: They constrain extreme results from stacked rules and prevent immediate buy-and-resell profit by default.

hints.buyMinMultiplier: Lower bound relative to the catalog price after currency conversion.
hints.buyMaxMultiplier: Upper bound relative to the catalog price after currency conversion.
hints.sellMinMultiplier: Lowest payout allowed relative to the catalog price.
hints.sellMaxMultiplier: Highest payout allowed relative to the catalog price.
hints.maxBuybackRatio: Prevents buyback from exceeding the same item's retail price.
hints.maxTemporaryPercent: Limits an accidentally extreme temporary adjustment.
hints.minimumAvailabilityChance: Lower bound for the calculated item availability chance.
hints.maximumAvailabilityChance: Upper bound for the calculated item availability chance.

pricing.modifiersDescription: Disable a rule globally here, or suppress it only inside a matching exception.

exceptions.title: Exceptions and special rules
exceptions.description: Higher priority runs first. Every non-empty criterion must match; values inside one criterion are alternatives.
exceptions.empty: No exceptions. The shop uses general market rules only.
exceptions.name: Rule name
exceptions.ignoreGuardrails: Allow this rule to bypass guardrails
exceptions.disableModifiers: Suppress general rules for this exception
exceptions.disableModifiersHint: Selected modifiers are skipped whenever this exception matches.

stunning.mechanics: Can impose temporary control penalties or trigger stun tests.

precise.mechanics: Usually improves hit chance, called shots, or critical reliability.

balanced.mechanics: Often reduces handling penalties and helps with parry/defense checks.

createShop.title: Add shop
createShop.description: Choose a business type, set the signboard and create a separate shop. The system will persist its profile and leave the offer empty.
createShop.help: Adds a separate shop, not another profile for the current shop. The new shop gets its own profile, status and stock. It does not copy the current offer.
createShop.chooseType: Choose a craft or kind of trade…
createShop.typeHelp: The business type is saved in the new shop profile and controls word selection when rolling a signboard. It does not force a name — you can still enter your own.
createShop.name: Shop name / signboard
createShop.nameHint: The name shown in the shop list and profile.
createShop.nameHelp: The name identifies this particular shop in the campaign. It does not set the business type or pricing policy. Two to six words are typical, for example “Under the Black Hammer”.
createShop.rollNameHelp: Rolls a non-repeating signboard suited to the selected craft and owner. A new shop starts with the default urban setting; after changing it you can roll more precisely in the profile. The result remains editable.
createShop.rollNameError: A name could not be rolled for the selected shop type.
createShop.ownerHelp: The owner selects the character or entity that settles the shop's transactions. It is not the shop profile and does not set its type. Choose npc for an independent merchant.
createShop.ownerNameHelp: The owner name is narrative text. It does not alter balances, prices or permissions. Example: “Master Ortwin”.
createShop.resultHint: The new shop profile opens after creation.

randomName.help: Rolls a new signboard from the current business type and profile setting. It does not change the type, prices or offer and does not save the form. Repeated rolls avoid duplicates within the craft.

help.signboardName: The signboard is the main name shown to players and in operation history. It does not change price or availability. A short name of 2–6 words is typical. Example: “Under the Brass Key”.
help.typeId: Shop type controls preferred categories, margin, buyback and availability. It does not change every good. Current: {value}. An armourer values armour more naturally than food.
help.ownerCode: The owner selects the character or entity that owns the shop and its purse. It does not set customer reputation. The current choice is used for saving and settlement. An independent trader can use the npc owner.
help.ownerName: The owner name is narrative text shown instead of a technical code. It does not alter prices, budget or access rights. A name and byname such as “Master Ortwin” is typical.
help.activity: An active shop can be used for trade and offer generation. Disabling it does not delete the profile or history and does not recalculate prices. A seasonal stall can be disabled after a fair.
help.aliases: Aliases are alternative signboard names separated by commas. They help search and narration but do not affect the economy. Zero to three regional or colloquial variants are typical.
help.worldProfileId: World profile sets purchasing power and availability with category-aware adjustments. Current: {value}. Standard is the typical baseline.
help.locationType: Location describes transport, local supply and imports. It is not a flat markup. Current: {value}. Ports aid imports; villages constrain luxuries.
help.legalStatus: Legality controls lawful, restricted and illegal goods plus risk premium. It does not change ordinary bread. Current: {value}.
help.wealthTier: Wealth defines shop capital, buyback limits and expensive stock share. It only modestly affects margin and does not make everything dearer. Current: {value}.
help.reputation: Base reputation is used when an actor has no individual relationship. It affects retail and buyback, not catalog price. Current: {value}.
help.seasonality: Seasonality affects matching categories only, not the whole offer. Current: {value}. Winter matters more for clothing and tools.
help.counterfeitRisk: Counterfeit risk is the chance of suspicious pricing for forgery-sensitive goods. It barely affects simple goods. Range 0–100%, current {value}%.
help.demandLevel: Demand changes a particular valuation, especially buyback. It does not replace stock. Current: {value}; normal is typical.
help.availabilityBias: Availability chance adjustment in percentage points. It does not directly change price. Typical range: −15 to +15; current {value} pp.
help.buybackBudget: Capital for the whole buyback batch. Empty uses wealth and does not increase retail price. Current: {value}.
help.maxBuybackItemValue: Maximum valuation of one buyback unit. Empty uses the wealth limit and does not cap retail. Current: {value}.
help.expensiveStockLimit: Limit for expensive generated stock. Empty derives it from wealth and does not remove manual goods. Current: {value}.
help.localCategories: Nearby goods cost less to transport and appear more often. Other categories are unaffected. Current: {value}.
help.importedCategories: Distant goods are easier at ports and gain transport premium off-route. Other goods are unaffected. Current: {value}.
help.actorReputation: A hero or party relationship overrides base reputation only for that actor and affects retail and buyback. Configured relationships: {count}.
help.autoTags: Tags are derived from shop type, place, law and other profile settings. They affect search and suggestion matching but do not change price themselves. The current set is shown beside this help and updates automatically.
help.marketEvents: A market event applies only within its dates, transaction modes and goods scope. It can change price and availability but not catalog price. A multiplier of 80–150% is typical. A closed route can raise import costs.
help.eventEnabled: This switch enables the rule without deleting its settings. A disabled event changes neither price nor availability. It is useful for preparing an event before a session.
help.eventName: The name helps the GM recognize the rule in the breakdown and history. It does not alter calculation. A cause such as “city siege” is typical.
help.eventType: The kind gives the event narrative meaning and starting values that can be refined. The type alone does not apply it to every good. Crop failure should usually target food.
help.eventDates: The dates define an inclusive start and end period. The rule is skipped outside it. The end date cannot precede the start date.
help.eventPrice: Price percentage is a multiplier for matching goods: 100% changes nothing and 120% raises price by 20%. It does not alter availability. The form allows a safe 10–500% range.
help.eventAvailability: Availability adds or removes percentage points for matching goods. It does not change price. −30 to +30 pp is typical; guardrails constrain the final result.
help.eventModes: Transaction mode decides whether the event applies to player purchases, shop buyback or both. It does not affect other operations. A shortage may raise both retail and buyback.
help.eventClasses: Classes limit the event to major item families. Empty means any class. Separate several values with commas. Example: weapons and armour during war.
help.eventGenres: Categories narrow the rule more precisely than class. Empty adds no restriction. Separate several values with commas. Example: grain during crop failure.
help.eventLocations: Locations make the rule apply only in a matching place. Empty means every location. A closed route may target a roadside shop.
help.eventItems: Identifiers restrict the event to specific templates. Empty does not restrict goods. This is a precise exception, such as one rationed medicine.
help.profileTools: These tools manage reusable settings, a profile copy, a portable file and history. They do not execute transactions or alter the offer without an explicit action.
help.profilePresets: A custom preset stores profile settings for reuse. It contains no campaign data or transaction history. For example, save a “poor winter stall” variant.
help.profileOperations: Duplication creates a separate profile, export prepares portable json, and import validates and saves settings through the api. Campaign-bound data is not copied.
help.profileHistory: History contains saved profile and policy revisions. Choosing one only loads its values into the form; the database changes after an explicit save.

iconPicker.selectionInstruction: Click another icon in the grid, review the change above, and confirm. Double-click selects it immediately.
iconPicker.twoFilesHint: Two square files of the same artwork are required: 42×42 and 144×144 px.
iconPicker.invalidUpload: Choose a PNG, JPEG or WebP file up to 4 MB.
iconPicker.invalidDimensions: The file must be a PNG, JPEG or WebP image sized exactly {size}×{size} px (max. 4 MB).
iconPicker.identitySectionHint: The name and description of this exact artwork
iconPicker.identitySectionHelp: Identity describes the icon file itself: how the artwork is named, what it depicts, and which source file it came from. It does not decide which items should receive this icon automatically.
iconPicker.classificationSectionHint: What the artwork depicts and where to find it
iconPicker.classificationSectionHelp: Classification organizes the library by what is visible in the artwork. Category is the main level and subcategory is the more precise description. These fields drive the icon-library filters.
iconPicker.matchingSectionHint: Which item data may receive this icon
iconPicker.matchingSectionHelp: Matching does not describe the icon's place in the library. It defines the item classes and item types for which the automatic resolver may suggest this artwork. For example, a bottle can be classified as Potion and matched to the Alchemy class and Healing type.
iconPicker.name: Icon name
iconPicker.nameHelp: A readable Polish name shown in the icon library. It does not rename items that use this icon.
iconPicker.sourceFileHelp: The original artwork file name. This read-only value identifies the source and can be searched.
iconPicker.descriptionHelp: A short description of what the artwork depicts and the visual context in which it should be used.
iconPicker.keywordsHelp: Polish words and phrases separated with commas. The resolver compares them with an item's name and description when suggesting this icon.
iconPicker.itemClassHelp: The broad item-data domain, such as Weapon, Alchemy, or Tool. It corresponds to the template's ITEM_CLASS field and is used for automatic suggestions.
iconPicker.itemGenreHelp: A more precise use within the item class, such as Healing, Shield, Melee, or Utility. It corresponds to ITEM_GENRE.
iconPicker.categoryHelp: The main group describing what is visible in the artwork. The list always shows every category. Changing it narrows subcategories and allowed matching values.
iconPicker.subcategoryHelp: A more precise artwork type within the selected category. The list depends only on the category, for example Clothing → Cloaks, Robes, Belts, or Bags.
iconPicker.legacyMultipleValues: This legacy record has multiple values. The editor shows the primary values and the next save will normalize every field to one value.

validation.nonNegative: Value must be greater than or equal to 0.
